"Triple Red 7s Multiplier" has six of ten top prizes left and is near the midpoint of its run. About half of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

The numbers for "Triple Red 7s Multiplier" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
802.headline: How much has sold

803.body:
"Triple Red 777s" has had no $1 million top prize claimed since we started watching it. Everyday prizes keep getting claimed, and fewer tickets are left each day. The number of tickets printed is fixed. Each day without a top prize claim leaves those prizes among fewer tickets.

If "Triple Red 777s" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
803.headline: No top prize claimed lately

804.body:
"Diamond Bingo" is near the midpoint of its run, with about two-thirds of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Everything here about "Diamond Bingo" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 19.
804.headline: How far along this game is

805.body:
"Multiply Your Money" has 207,928 prizes of $5 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $5,000 prize, with eight left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Everything here about "Multiply Your Money" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 19.
805.headline: The prize table, line by line

806.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "Win $50, $100 or $200", about half are still unsold. The game is about halfway through its run, with 9,502 of 18,893 top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The table below shows the full count for "Win $50, $100 or $200", with every prize level included.
806.headline: Early stage or late

807.body:
"Ravens X2" is down to two top prizes after a $20,000 winner was claimed last week. The game started with four top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

If you play "Ravens X2" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
807.headline: Fewer $20,000 prizes left

808.body:
The most common win left on "Ravens X10" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and two of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

The numbers for "Ravens X10" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
808.headline: A close look at the prizes

809.body:
"Gold Bar Bingo" has six of seven top prizes left and is about halfway through its run. About a third of the tickets are already sold. As a game goes on, the same prizes are spread across fewer tickets. Right now, a larger share of the top prizes is left than of the tickets, which is a good sign.

Tomorrow's count on "Gold Bar Bingo" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
809.headline: How much has sold

810.body:
On "In the Green", one $50,000 top prize was claimed earlier this week. That leaves five of the original seven. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

The numbers for "In the Green" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.
810.headline: A top prize was just claimed

811.body:
The prize money on "Extreme Green" leans toward small, frequent prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay out often, in small amounts. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Today's free summary of "Extreme Green" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
811.headline: What type of game it is

812.body:
One of Loose Change®'s top prizes was claimed last week. A player in Maryland won $1,000. The game started with 24 top prizes and now has fifteen top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

Tomorrow's count on "Loose Change®" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
812.headline: A player won a top prize

813.body:
One of The Price is Right™'s top prizes was claimed two weeks ago. A player in Maryland won $50,000. The game started with six top prizes and now has four top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

If "The Price is Right™" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
813.headline: Fewer $50,000 prizes left

814.body:
A $100,000 top prize on "High Voltage" was claimed earlier this week. The game started with eight top prizes and has six top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

If "High Voltage" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
814.headline: Someone claimed a $100,000 prize

815.body:
"$100,000 Crossword" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. Of its unclaimed prize money, most is in wins under $1,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

The numbers for "$100,000 Crossword" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
815.headline: How the prize money is divided

816.body:
A $50,000 top prize on "Deluxe Crossword" was claimed over a week ago. The game started with eight top prizes and has seven top prizes left. The prize table has today's count for every prize level.

If "Deluxe Crossword" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
816.headline: Top prize count went down

817.body:
"Hello Money!" is down to six top prizes after a $50,000 winner was claimed last week. The game started with seven top prizes. Know that before you buy, because a change in top prizes changes the whole game.

The table below shows the full count for "Hello Money!", with every prize level included.
817.headline: Another top prize was claimed

818.body:
The most common win left on "10X Cash" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $1,000, and 38 of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything here about "10X Cash" comes from official Maryland lottery numbers, current through October 19.
818.headline: A close look at the prizes

819.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "30X Cash", about three-quarters is in wins under $5,000. The game is a game built around small prizes that are won often. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

How far "30X Cash" is through its run does not decide anything by itself. It changes how closely to look at the other numbers.

The table below shows the full count for "30X Cash", with every prize level included.
819.headline: How this game pays out

820.body:
"Cozy Cash" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $1 game with 35 top prizes of $500. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

The numbers for "Cozy Cash" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
820.headline: New in stores

821.body:
"Season's Greetings" just went on sale in Maryland. The game has ten full prize levels with six top prizes of $10,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

If "Season's Greetings" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
821.headline: First day on sale

822.body:
"Peppermint Payout" is new from the Maryland Lottery. It is a $3 game with six top prizes of $30,000. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

Tomorrow's count on "Peppermint Payout" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
822.headline: A new game is here

823.body:
"Holly-Day Cash" just reached Maryland stores with seven top prizes of $50,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

Everything above about "Holly-Day Cash" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
823.headline: A brand-new game to watch

824.body:
"Winter Multiplier" has joined the Maryland lineup at $10 with nine top prizes of $100,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

If "Winter Multiplier" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
824.headline: Brand new, no claims yet

825.body:
Only a small slice of the tickets for "Win $100, $200 or $500" have been sold. The game is early in its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, neither the tickets nor the top prizes are running out faster than the other.

Everything above about "Win $100, $200 or $500" comes from the Maryland Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
